html:
On 8 January 1297 François Grimaldi, a Genoese exile, took the fortress on the Rock of Monaco, supposedly by disguising himself as a Franciscan friar. His family, the Grimaldis, have ruled Monaco for most of the time since.

The Grimaldis were one of the great families of Genoa, driven out in its factional wars. They lost and retook the rock several times before holding it for good from 1419. The friar with a sword is still on Monaco's coat of arms.

Monaco survived as a tiny state under the protection of Spain, then France. It lost Menton and Roquebrune in 1861, leaving only the rock and the coast around it, and turned to the casino to live. Today Prince Albert II rules. See Monaco.
